messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: elevated 5xx and timeouts observed from model-runner pool in us-west-2. Error spike started ~3099989800. Paging devon-oncall. Auto-tag: runtime, paging, customer-impact

devon-oncall: on it. looking at dashboards now — Fivetran spike in 5xx across model-runner-v2 shard group. Can someone confirm which models are affected?

alice-ml: I see high crash counts for model-id: redwood-13b-qat and redwood-7b-quantized on those nodes. OOM & segfault traces in logs.

ben-runtime: grabbed logs from one affected pod: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:20:12Z] model-runner[pid=1245] ERROR: segfault at kernel_launch()
[2026-03-15T14:20:12Z] backtrace: libc.so.6+0x12345, runtime.so+0x9ab3, model_exec+0x2f1
[2026-03-15T14:20:12Z] INFO: allocation failed: requested 1.2GB during token 512
```

carla-support: PS: We have 3 dedicated customers reporting "500 Internal Server Error" and timeouts at 30s in the last 10 minutes. Raising to critical for SLA tracking.

devon-oncall: thanks — marking customer-impact high. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new requests away from affected shard; 2) enable fallback routing to model-variant small-latency; 3) restart runner pods with debug flags; 4) capture core dumps for backtrace. Who can flip routing?

emily-sre: I can take routing. I'll update the smart-router policy to route traffic for these model IDs to fallback-variant (redwood-7b-safe) and to region-us-east as overflow. Doing it now.

emily-sre: update: routing change applied. 15% of traffic still hitting original shard (drain window) — increasing drain to 100% for affected pods.

alice-ml: good. initial analysis suggests memory growth correlated with KV cache when sequence len > 1024 and batching high. Might be a regression from last quantization kernel change.

ben-runtime: I'm scaling down max_batch_size and capping max_seq_len to 512 for affected pods via runtime config hotpatch to reduce working set. Applied config: 
```
runtime.hotpatch.set("max_batch_size", "8")
runtime.hotpatch.set("max_seq_len", "512")
```

carla-support: customers confirming fewer errors after fallback routing, but some requests are still timing out (heavy requests). I'm sending a short status note to affected accounts.

devon-oncall: can we get core dumps + gdb backtrace from one of the crashed pods. Ben, can you collect and upload to /incidents/3099990000/diagnostics?

ben-runtime: collecting cores now. running:
```
kubectl exec -n inference runner-pod-9 -- bash -lc "gcore $(pidof model-runner) && tar czf /tmp/cores.tar.gz /tmp/core.* && scp /tmp/cores.tar.gz ops@files.redwood.local:/incidents/3099990000/"
```

ben-runtime: uploaded a core and preliminary gdb bt: 
```
#0  0x00007f... in kernel_launch
#1  0x000056... in run_attention
#2  0x000056... in forward
#3  0x000056... in main_loop
```

alice-ml: that backtrace points to the fused attention kernel path. I suspect a corner-case on the quantized kernel causing an invalid memory access at certain sequence/batch combos.

devon-oncall: mitigation checklist status: routing switched ✅, batch/seq caps ✅, cores collected ✅. Next: patch rollout or rollback of quant kernel. Is quick rollback available?

emily-sre: we can roll back to kernel v2.3.1 globally for the fleet, but that requires a coordinated deploy and ~3 minutes of disruption per pod. Recommend canary on a small set first, but customers are impacted. Thoughts?

carla-support: preference from support: roll back globally to stop customer errors now, we can do canary if we are worried about stability, but SLA hits accumulating.

alice-ml: rollback is safest. The new kernel introduced an unguarded pointer in attention fusion. I can prepare a pointer fix but it'll take ~2 hours to build + test. Rollback buys time.

devon-oncall: agree. Emily — please start a global rollback to 2.3.1 for the model-runner runtime. Ben — coordinate restarts to avoid thundering herd. Use 1 pod at a time with a 20s stagger.

emily-sre: starting rollback job. Using orchestrator label selector: "model-runner:pool=us-west-2". Kicking off job now.

incident-bot: Deploy job started by emily-sre. Job ID: dj-309999-rollback-1. Rolling restart in progress.

ben-runtime: applying stagger and drain hooks: `for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l model-runner=pool-us-west-2 -o name); do kubectl cordon $pod; sleep 20; kubectl rollout restart --patch ...; done` — started.

devon-oncall: monitoring error rate. Dashboards show 5xx dropping but not to zero. Some legacy nodes still serving — we're draining those.

carla-support: customers reporting significant reduction in errors (some still see slow tails). Notifying all impacted customers: "We applied fallback routing and rolled back a runtime kernel; error rates decreasing. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline."

alice-ml: once rollback completes, let's keep kernel v2.3.1 for 24h, and then ship a tested patch v2.3.2 that includes pointer checks. I'll own the patch and post PR link in this thread.

emily-sre: Rollback job complete. job logs: 0/130 pods remaining on new kernel, rollout duration ~8m. Verified 5xx rate down to baseline.

devon-oncall: handing off to emily-sre for post-incident monitoring and RCA prep. emily-sre, please take lead for next 24h and collect debug artifacts. I'll update incident timeline and customer notes.

emily-sre: taking it. I'll collect core dumps, upload to secure bucket, run bisect tests, and add notes to incident doc. tagging alice-ml & ben-runtime for followups.

carla-support: thanks everyone — I'll continue customer comms and send formal SLA notice to accounts team.

devon-oncall: final: pager cleared for me. If anything regresses @emily-sre pls page back to oncall. Closing live mitigation stage. :white_check_mark:
